Work_Order.task_description: Read the whole destination file. For each function state what is processed, where inputs originate, where outputs go next, and its purpose. Use at most 512 characters. Only fill function_description and function_complete; preserve every other field and its order. Leave uncertainty incomplete. Run shakti_work_order validate before returning this to the assigned supervisor. Never edit destination sources. Import into the parsed list before running shakti_diff; compare rendered lists, never this work order.

SECTION.function_description: Folds the eight bytes of v into the incoming FNV state h, multiplying after each byte. eye_intake hash builders call it for dimensions, pixels, sequence pins, and block or stream chaining; the returned hash becomes the next deterministic state.

Consumes the caller supplied string byte by byte through fnv1, starting from h. sight_hash, sight_record, and intake use the returned state to bind labels, formats, names, stages, and error paths into deterministic sight or stream hashes.

Builds one sight identity from the loaded global pixel grid plus caller supplied name and format. It folds dimensions, then visits every pixel in canonical Bayer 4x4 rank order; intake passes the resulting hash to sight_record for the ledger and pin chain.

Reads an already opened 8x8 text glyph after its magic line, takes the TEXT value as name, and loads dot or hash rows into global PX with 8 columns. It returns success when a name and at least one complete 8-row character were found; intake then hashes and records that grid.

Reads an opened 64x64 binary glyph after its magic line, parses ASCII, and copies 64-bit rows into global PX. On exactly 64 accepted rows it emits name ascii_NNN and success; intake then counts ink, hashes the grid, and records it.

SECTION.function_input: const char *name, const char *fmt, uint64_t hash, uint64_t ink, const char *wav
SECTION.function_description: Receives a validated glyph identity, format, sight hash, ink count, and sound binding from intake. It appends a sight ledger line, derives its ticket pin, advances stream and block pins, and every ten tickets writes a block seal that seeds the next block.

SECTION.function_input: const char *path, const char *fmt, const char *wav
SECTION.function_description: Processes one manifest tuple path, format, and wav. It opens the glyph, selects the loader from the file magic, records missing or bad paths into the stream pin, counts loaded ink pixels, computes the sight hash, increments glyph_count, and hands the result to sight_record.

Initializes the eye intake run by seeding stream_pin and block_pin with the FNV basis and clearing ticket, block, sequence, and glyph counters. The harness calls it before eye_intake_run so later ledger and accessor outputs begin from a deterministic state.

Opens GLYPH_MANIFEST.txt and processes each line containing path, format, and wav through intake in manifest order. It closes the manifest and returns glyph_count to the harness, while intake and sight_record build SIGHT.ndx and the in-memory pin chain.

Appends the current stream_pin as the final stream record in SIGHT.ndx when the ledger can be opened. It is called after manifest intake so the completed sight ledger carries the accumulated stream proof; it deliberately returns no status.

Returns the current global sight stream_pin accumulated by sight_record and missing or bad intake paths. The harness reads it after the run and seal for reporting or comparison; this accessor does not alter intake state.

Returns block_count, which sight_record increments whenever ten sight tickets close a block. The intake harness consumes the value after processing to report how many complete sealed blocks were produced; no state is changed.

Returns glyph_count, incremented by intake only after a glyph loads successfully and its sight hash is ready for recording. It exposes the completed capture count to callers without changing the ledger or hash state.

Checks whether a caller supplied text pointer is non-null and nonempty. The file uses this result as the common presence gate for names, references, claims, and schema labels before copying, accepting, or serializing them.

Validates destination, capacity, and source text, rejects a source that would not fit, then copies it including the terminator. Plan and geometry builders use its success result before committing fixed-size names and evidence references to their structures.

Checks nonempty text for XML-safe control content, allowing tab, line feed, and carriage return while rejecting other bytes below 0x20. XML writers call it before emitting stored references or person-reading fields so invalid control text is refused before output.

Tests whether an evidence enum lies from SHAKTI_EVIDENCE_NONE through SHAKTI_EVIDENCE_VERIFIED. Consequence, option, and person-reading validation consume the boolean result before accepting evidence values into later choice or XML processing.

Classifies only TAUGHT, OBSERVED, or VERIFIED evidence as authoritative. Condition creation, consequence comparison, filtering, and geometry sister readings use this gate so claims, creative proposals, and NONE cannot satisfy evidence-required decisions.

Accepts only the three defined truth states UNKNOWN, FALSE, or TRUE. consequence_valid uses the returned boolean to reject malformed reachability values before a consequence is stored in the choice matrix.

Checks that an option kind lies within the defined ACTION through ALTERNATIVE enum range. shakti_choice_add_option uses it before allocating an option slot, preventing out-of-range kinds from entering the plan.
Accepts only byte values 0 or 1. consequence_valid applies it to reversible and protected_boundary_breach so later filtering and weighting operate on canonical boolean state.

Validates a proposed consequence before storage: present flag, truth, evidence, confidence bound, boolean flags, and evidence reference must be valid, and NONE or CREATIVE evidence is refused. shakti_choice_set_consequence uses the result before copying the item into the plan matrix.

Computes left minus right into the caller output only when the pointer is valid and signed 64-bit subtraction cannot overflow. shakti_choice_delta and shakti_choice_weigh_range consume its OK, REFUSED, or OVERFLOW status instead of performing unsafe arithmetic.

Receives a plan from the caller, clears the entire structure when non-null, and sets baseline_index to -1 to mark that no no-action baseline exists yet. All plan-building tests call it before adding conditions, horizons, options, claims, or consequences.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_choice_plan_t *plan, const char *name, shakti_choice_evidence_t evidence, const char *evidence_ref
SECTION.function_description: Adds one named condition to an open plan only with authoritative evidence, a reference, free capacity, and no duplicate name. It safely copies fields, increments condition_count, and returns the new index used later to address consequence cells.

Adds a future horizon to an open plan from caller supplied ticks and name. It requires capacity and rejects duplicate tick distances or names, stores the values, increments horizon_count, and returns the index later used to place and compare consequences.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_choice_plan_t *plan, shakti_option_kind_t kind, const char *name, shakti_choice_evidence_t discovery_evidence, const char *discovery_ref
SECTION.function_description: Adds a uniquely named option to an open plan after validating kind, discovery evidence, reference, capacity, and the single-baseline rule. It copies the option, records baseline_index for NO_ACTION, increments option_count, and returns the new index for consequence assignment.

Stores caller supplied claim text and speaker reference while enumeration is open and claim capacity remains. It safely copies both fields, increments claim_count, and returns the index; shakti_choice_filter later exposes the accumulated claim count as unverified_claim_count.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_choice_plan_t *plan, size_t option_index, size_t condition_index, size_t horizon_index, const shakti_consequence_t *consequence
SECTION.function_description: Places a validated consequence into the selected option, condition, and horizon cell of an open plan. It rejects null plans, closed enumeration, out-of-range indices, or invalid consequence evidence and flags; accepted data becomes the matrix later read by filtering and delta calculations.

Locks plan enumeration after requiring at least two options, one condition, one horizon, a no-action baseline, and a nonempty enumeration reference. It copies that reference and sets enumeration_closed so later additions are refused and filtering can begin.

Evaluates every option consequence in a closed plan against policy severity and confidence gates. Unsupported or unknown cells make an option EVIDENCE_OPEN; reachable authoritative irreversible protected catastrophic harm filters it; otherwise it survives. It returns counts and baseline status in result.

SECTION.function_input: const shakti_choice_plan_t *plan, size_t option_index, size_t condition_index, size_t horizon_index, int64_t *delta
SECTION.function_description: Compares one option consequence with the no-action baseline at the same condition and horizon. Both cells must be present, reachable TRUE, and authoritative; then subtract_i64 writes choice value minus baseline value to delta. OPEN or arithmetic status returns to survivor analysis.

SECTION.function_input: int64_t best, int64_t worst, int reversible
SECTION.function_description: Turns caller supplied best and worst deltas into a bounded deliberation-beat count. It validates ordering and the reversible flag, computes spread safely, multiplies irreversible spread by the irreversible factor with overflow protection, then repeatedly applies the ladder divisor up to the deliberation limit.

SECTION.function_input: const shakti_choice_plan_t *plan, const shakti_choice_result_t *result, int64_t *best_delta, int64_t *worst_delta
SECTION.function_description: Scans surviving nonbaseline options across every condition and horizon, obtains usable deltas from shakti_choice_delta, tracks best and worst, and notes whether all compared consequences are reversible. It writes the range to caller outputs and returns the beat count from shakti_choice_weigh_range.

Maps an evidence enum received from choice or geometry records to its stable text label NONE, CREATIVE, CLAIM, TAUGHT, OBSERVED, VERIFIED, or INVALID. XML writers consume the returned literal when serializing evidence attributes.

Converts an option-kind enum into the stable labels ACTION, NO_ACTION, WAIT, REFUSE, TEACH_ME, ALTERNATIVE, or INVALID. It provides a textual seam for callers that need to report a stored option kind without changing plan state.

Converts an option-status enum produced by filtering into UNCHECKED, SURVIVES, FILTERED, EVIDENCE_OPEN, or INVALID. The returned constant string is for downstream reporting and does not alter the result structure.

Maps a sister enum to DESTROYER, PRESERVER, CREATOR, or INVALID. shakti_geometry_write_xml uses the returned label for each evidence-bound sister reading written under the two frames of a use placement.

Clears a caller supplied geometry schema when the pointer is non-null. Tests call it before defining frames and poles, leaving every definition unlocked until explicit evidence-backed definitions are added.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_geometry_schema_t *schema, unsigned int frame, const char *name, const char *question, const char *evidence_ref, int locked
SECTION.function_description: Defines one frame slot from caller name, question, evidence reference, and required locked flag. It refuses invalid indices, already locked frames, missing text, or copy failures; on success it commits a locked definition that shakti_geometry_ready later verifies.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_geometry_schema_t *schema, unsigned int pole, const char *name, const char *evidence_ref, int locked
SECTION.function_description: Defines one pole slot from caller name and evidence reference with a required locked flag. It refuses invalid or previously locked slots and bad text, then commits the locked pole; shakti_geometry_ready later requires both pole definitions and distinct names.

Checks that every frame is locked with name, question, and evidence reference, that frame names are unique, and that both poles are locked with names and evidence references whose names differ. Placement and XML writing require this true result before using the schema.

SECTION.function_input: unsigned int frame_a, unsigned int frame_b, unsigned int pole, unsigned int *vertex
SECTION.function_description: Maps two distinct valid frame indices plus a pole to one of 20 fixed geometry vertices through the symmetric pair table. It writes the vertex to the caller pointer and returns OK only for a mapped value below 20; placement uses this to locate a use event.

SECTION.function_input: const shakti_geometry_schema_t *schema, shakti_use_geometry_t *use, const char *source_memory_ref, const char *use_event_ref, unsigned int frame_a, unsigned int frame_b, unsigned int pole
SECTION.function_description: Creates a use placement from a ready schema, source-memory and use-event references, two frames, and a pole. It resolves the vertex, copies references, stores frame indices in ascending order, and writes the completed placement to use for sister readings and XML serialization.

SECTION.function_input: shakti_use_geometry_t *use, unsigned int frame_slot, shakti_sister_t sister, int64_t value, shakti_choice_evidence_t evidence, const char *evidence_ref
SECTION.function_description: Stores one evidence-bound sister value in a placed use for a selected frame slot. It requires a valid slot and sister, authoritative evidence, and reference, then marks the reading present; geometry XML later requires all three sisters for both frames.

Writes caller text to an output stream as XML character data, rejecting forbidden control bytes and escaping ampersand, angle brackets, quotes, and apostrophes. Geometry and person-record writers use its success result so stored text is emitted safely or the record is refused.

Serializes a ready use geometry record to the caller stream after validating references, frames, pole, vertex, and frame names. It requires all six sister readings to be present with authoritative evidence, returns OPEN if they are incomplete, and writes source, event, placement, frames, and readings as XML.

Writes a visible person-reading record from the caller structure only when its id, visibility flag, evidence, and all text fields are valid. It XML-escapes the subject, history, state, obligation, and conclusion and returns OK only after the complete record reaches the output stream.

SECTION.function_input: FILE *output, uint64_t reading_id, const char *subject, const char *correction, const char *evidence_ref
SECTION.function_description: Writes a correction tied to a nonzero reading id from caller subject, correction text, and evidence reference. It validates all text for XML controls, escapes it through xml_text, and emits a complete person_correction record for downstream preservation of the subject's correction.

Creates GLYPH_MANIFEST.txt in fixed order from the file's built-in sound names and punctuation codes, then ASCII 32 through 127. It writes 8x8 paths with wav bindings or NONE followed by 64x64 sight-only paths; main supplies this manifest to eye_intake_run.

Runs the eye-intake harness: removes the old sight ledger, writes the deterministic manifest, initializes and runs intake, seals SIGHT.ndx, then reports glyph count, block count, stream pin, the first six sight records, and total sight lines. It returns 0 after the diagnostic pass.

Folds the eight bytes of v into an incoming FNV state h and returns the next state. main feeds retained cube vertices, exact dodecahedron coordinates, search count, and match count through it to produce deterministic incidence and proof pins.

Constructs the exact Z[phi] value a plus b times phi from two signed integer coefficients. The arithmetic helpers return values through this constructor, and those pairs flow into coordinate and squared-distance calculations without floating point.

Subtracts the a and b coefficients of two exact Z[phi] values and returns the resulting pair through zp_of. dist2 uses it to form coordinate differences between two dodecahedron vertices before squaring them.
Adds corresponding coefficients of two Z[phi] values and returns the exact pair. dist2 chains this helper to sum the three squared coordinate differences that feed edge and cube classification.
Compares both integer coefficients of two Z[phi] values for exact equality. is_edge and is_cube use the boolean result to classify squared distances without rounding or tolerance.
Multiplies two Z[phi] values exactly, reducing phi squared to phi plus one so the product remains an integer coefficient pair. dist2 uses it to square coordinate differences before summing them.

Populates global V with the 20 scaled dodecahedron vertices using exact values 1, phi, inverse-phi, zero, and their negatives. main calls it before any geometry test; dist2, edge checks, cube search, pole checks, and proof hashing all consume V.

Reads vertices p and q from global V, subtracts each exact coordinate, squares the differences in Z[phi], and returns their sum as exact squared distance. is_edge, check_solid, and is_cube use this value to test geometric relationships.

Classifies two distinct vertex indices as a dodecahedron edge when dist2 equals the exact edge square 8 minus 4 phi. Face enumeration and connectivity checks consume this boolean to build and verify the solid's edge graph.

Enumerates every 5-vertex subset, identifies induced five-cycles using is_edge, and accumulates face, vertex-face, and edge-face incidence. It expects 12 faces, three faces per vertex, and two per edge, prints the checks, and returns true only when all hold.

Verifies the generated coordinates form the intended dodecahedron edge graph: each vertex must have degree three at the exact edge distance, total edges must be 30, the graph must reach all 20 vertices, and check_faces must pass. It prints each result and returns their conjunction.

Tests one 8-vertex subset from search as an inscribed cube using exact squared distances 4, 8, and 12. It requires global pair counts 12 edges, 12 face diagonals, 4 space diagonals, no other distances, and per-vertex counts 3, 3, and 1; the boolean returns to search.

Enumerates every 8-vertex subset of the 20 vertices in lexicographic order and sends each to is_cube. It counts all subsets and cube matches, retains up to five matching vertex sets in global CUBE, increments cube_count, and returns the number of subsets tried to main.

Compares every pair of retained cubes and counts which global vertices occur in both 8-vertex sets. It prints each overlap and expects exactly two shared vertices per pair; the final boolean goes to main as the frame-pair incidence check.

Reads vertices p and q and returns true only when every a and b coefficient of q is the exact negative of the corresponding coefficient of p. check_poles uses this exact coordinate test on the two vertices shared by each cube pair.

For every retained cube pair, collects the vertices present in both cubes, requires exactly two, and tests that pair with is_antipodal. It prints each frame-pair pole result and returns true only when every checked pair consists of exact opposite vertices.

Formats one exact Z[phi] pair directly to stdout, choosing integer-only, phi-only, or combined coefficient form. main calls it while reporting all generated vertex coordinates; it changes no geometry state.

Orchestrates the exact frame proof: builds and prints 20 vertices, validates the dodecahedron, exhaustively finds cubes, checks per-vertex incidence, cube-pair overlap, and antipodal poles, then hashes incidence and proof data. It returns 0 only when the solid, five cubes, pair laws, poles, and twice-per-vertex incidence all pass.

Runs the paint harness: creates the output directory, clears PAINT.ndx, initializes paint state, emits 11 color swabs, all built-in sound-name glyphs in black on white, and four colored letter demos. It seals the ledger, reports completed count, blocks, and stream pin, then prints selected swab and R, B, G, Y ledger records.

Folds the eight bytes of v into incoming FNV state h and returns the next state. fnv_str, paint_hash, and paint_record use it for painted pixel identities, ticket pins, block chaining, and the accumulated paint stream pin.

Consumes a caller string byte by byte through fnv1 starting from h. paint_hash and paint_record use the returned state to bind painted labels, glyph names, color names, and stream record prefixes into deterministic hashes.

Searches the fixed 11-swatch palette for the caller supplied color name and returns its constant hex string or NULL. paint_emit uses it to validate and label ink and ground colors, while paint_swab uses it to reject unknown solid colors before creating a grid.

Reads an opened 8x8 text glyph after its magic line, captures the TEXT name, and loads dot or hash rows into global PX with eight columns. It returns success when a name and at least one complete 8-row character are present; paint_glyph then sends the grid to paint_emit.

Reads an opened binary glyph after its magic line, parses the ASCII number, and copies complete 64-bit rows into global PX. With exactly 64 rows it returns success and name ascii_NNN; paint_glyph then passes that loaded grid to paint_emit.

SECTION.function_input: const char *name, int rows, int cols
SECTION.function_description: Receives validated row and column dimensions from paint_swab, sets the global pixel dimensions, and fills every cell with 1 to form a solid grid. The name parameter is intentionally unused; paint_swab supplies the swab name separately to paint_emit.

SECTION.function_input: const char *name, const char *ink, const char *ground
SECTION.function_description: Builds a painted sight hash from the loaded global grid plus glyph name, ink, and ground. It folds the painted label, colors, dimensions, and pixels visited in Bayer 4x4 rank order; paint_emit passes the resulting identity to the painted ledger.

SECTION.function_input: const char *name, const char *ink, const char *ground, uint64_t hash, const char *wav
SECTION.function_description: Receives a painted name, colors, hash, and wav from paint_emit, appends a PAINT.ndx record, and derives a sequence ticket pin from name and hash. It advances stream and block pins and writes a block seal every ten tickets, then seeds the next block from the prior block pin.

SECTION.function_input: const char *name, const char *ink, const char *ground, const char *wav
SECTION.function_description: Emits one loaded or synthetic grid as a painted card. It validates both colors, computes paint_hash, writes SHAKTI_PAINTED_GRID_V1 with named colors, hex values, dimensions, and pixel rows, increments paint_count, and hands the identity to paint_record; callers receive 1 on success or 0 on failure.

Seeds paint stream_pin and block_pin with the FNV basis and clears block tickets, block count, sequence, and completed-paint count. The harness calls it before swabs or glyphs so paint_emit and paint_record begin from deterministic state.

SECTION.function_input: const char *path, const char *fmt, const char *ink, const char *ground, const char *wav
SECTION.function_description: Processes one caller glyph path, declared format, ink, ground, and wav. It opens the file, clears PX, checks the magic and matching 8x8 or 64x64 format, loads the grid, then passes its name and requested colors to paint_emit; the returned 1 or 0 reports the complete paint operation.

SECTION.function_input: const char *color, int rows, int cols
SECTION.function_description: Creates a solid color card from caller color and dimensions. It requires a palette color and bounds rows and columns to the pixel store, names the card swab_color, fills PX through make_swab, and sends it to paint_emit with identical ink and ground and no sound binding.

Appends the current paint stream_pin as the final stream line in PAINT.ndx when the ledger can be opened. The harness calls it after all paint emissions so the ledger carries its accumulated stream proof; the best-effort function returns no status.

Returns the global stream_pin accumulated from every paint ticket by paint_record. The harness reads it after sealing for deterministic reporting or comparison; the accessor does not modify paint state.

Returns block_count, incremented by paint_record each time ten paint tickets close a block. The harness consumes the value after painting to report complete block seals without changing the ledger or counters.

Returns paint_count, which paint_emit increments only after a painted grid file is written successfully. It exposes the number of completed painted cards to callers while leaving all hash, block, and ledger state unchanged.

SECTION.function_input: int64_t value, unsigned int severity, unsigned int confidence, int reversible, int boundary, shakti_truth_t reachable, shakti_choice_evidence_t evidence, const char *evidence_ref
SECTION.function_description: Builds a test shakti_consequence_t from caller value, severity, confidence, flags, reachability, evidence, and reference. It zeroes the record, marks it present, copies all fields after asserting the reference fits, and returns the value for test scenarios to pass into set_one.

Places one test consequence into condition 0 and horizon 0 for the supplied option index. It asserts the option is nonnegative and that shakti_choice_set_consequence returns OK, giving scenario tests a compact path from constructed consequences into the plan matrix.

Exercises refusal and arithmetic invariants: invalid ranges and reversible flags, overflow, equal range, irreversible weighting, non-authoritative condition evidence, duplicate no-action baseline, and premature enumeration close. Assertions consume API return codes; a pass line is printed only after the checks execute.

Builds a three-option ice-cream plan with one verified condition and horizon, assigns safe reachable consequences, closes and filters it, and asserts all options survive including baseline. It then checks survivor deltas of best 5 and worst -2 produce two deliberation beats and prints the scenario result.

Builds a dog-hazard plan with six visible options. Catastrophic irreversible protected harm is assigned to no-action, wait, refuse, and teach paths, while direct crossing and mud remain reachable alternatives. It asserts filtering removes four paths, baseline is filtered, two survive, and survivor deltas 98 to 100 yield one beat.

Constructs baseline plus three catastrophic-harm cases to isolate the filter gates. It asserts authoritative reachable harm above severity and confidence is FILTERED, low-confidence harm is EVIDENCE_OPEN, and verified unreachable harm SURVIVES, confirming severity, confidence, reachability, and evidence act together.

Stores a pressure-sale statement as a claim, then builds verified safe no-action and refuse options. After closing enumeration it asserts a late claim is refused, filtering preserves both options, baseline survives, and the original claim is counted as one unverified claim rather than becoming urgency or consequence evidence.

Turns a temporary output stream into a caller buffer for assertions: it validates arguments, flushes writes, seeks to the start, reads up to capacity minus one, and adds a terminator. Geometry and person-reading tests use the resulting text to inspect emitted XML.

Tests the geometry seam from empty schema through XML. It locks five frames and two poles, rejects redefinition, proves 10 frame pairs times two poles cover 20 unique vertices, places one use at vertex 9, fills both frames with all three authoritative sister readings, writes XML, and checks the expected labels and placement.

Builds a person reading and proves visibility is required before serialization, then writes the visible record plus a subject correction and checks XML escaping and reading linkage. A second record containing a forbidden control byte is refused, and the test asserts nothing was written to that invalid stream.

Runs the complete choice-consequence test sequence in source order: refusal and weighing checks, ice-cream, dog and mud, severity-confidence, pressure claim, geometry-sister, and visible person-reading cases. Assertions enforce each invariant; after all return it prints the verdict and exits 0.
